title: Transformation of Bacillus subtilis with DNA from natural donor cell lysis
author: James P. Finn IV
materials: If filtration is necessary (see Before Start):
If working in 18 mm glass test tubes:
Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.

steps.title: Prepare Donor and Recipient Strains
steps.instruction: Streak out donor and recipient strains onto LB agar plates to obtain fresh, single colonies.

substeps.instruction: Streak donor strain onto LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotics; incubate at 37 °C for approximately 18 hours.
Streak recipient strain onto LB agar plate; incubate at 30 °C for at most 42 hours.

steps.title: Prepare 1x MC Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare the 1x MC medium according to the required volume.

substeps.instruction: For 1 mL: Mix 900 µL sterile ddH2O, 3 µL 1M MgSO4, and 100 µL 10x MC (stored at -30 °C).
For 400 µL: Mix 360 µL sterile ddH2O, 1.2 µL 1M MgSO4, and 40 µL 10x MC (stored at -30 °C).

steps.title: Inoculate and Grow Donor Culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate the donor strain in 1x MC medium and incubate to allow cell lysis.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL of 1x MC medium in 18 mm sterile glass test tubes (or 200 µL in standard 96-well plates / 400 µL in square deep-well 96-well plates).
Inoculate the medium with one donor colony using an inoculating stick or pipette tip.
Vortex at setting 3 to 4 for 10 seconds (if using sticks) and remove the stick.
Incubate at 37 °C for 20-24 hours with aeration (use a roller drum for 18 mm tubes, or a platform shaker at 350 rpm with an aeration seal for 96-well plates).

steps.title: Inoculate and Grow Recipient Culture
steps.instruction: Prepare the recipient culture four hours before the end of the donor incubation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 mL of 1x MC medium in 18 mm sterile glass test tubes (or 200 µL in standard 96-well plates / 400 µL in square deep-well 96-well plates).
Inoculate with one recipient colony using a sterile inoculation stick or pipette tip.
Incubate at 37 °C for 4 hours with aeration using the same methods as the donor culture.

steps.title: Prepare Donor DNA Source
steps.instruction: Extract the donor DNA from the culture via filtration or aspiration.

substeps.instruction: Option A (Filtration): Aliquot 1 mL of donor culture into a 1.7 mL microfuge tube, spin at 21,000 x g for 1 minute, and transfer the supernatant to a new tube without disrupting the pellet.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm PES filter (cellulose acetate or nylon are also acceptable).
Option B (Aspiration): Aspirate directly from the donor culture and filter through a 0.22 µm filter.
Store the resulting filtrate (donor DNA source) at room temperature or -30 °C.

steps.title: Perform Transformation
steps.instruction: Mix the recipient cells with the donor DNA filtrate.

substeps.instruction: For glass tube format: Transfer 200 µL of recipient to a sterile 13 mm glass tube and add 10 µL of donor filtrate/lysate.
For 96-well plate format: Transfer 200 µL of recipient to a fresh well and add 10 µL of donor filtrate/lysate.
Incubate the transformation mixtures at 37 °C for 2 hours with aeration (for 13 mm tubes, use 18 mm tubes with small caps or 1 mL pipette tips to hold them).

steps.title: Plate and Incubate Transformants
steps.instruction: Dilute the transformation cultures and plate them on selective media.

substeps.instruction: Dilute transformation cultures 1:10 and 1:100.
Dispense 100 µL to 200 µL of the dilution onto appropriate selective agar plates.
Spread cells evenly using 4-5 beads per petri plate, ensuring the liquid does not sit too long on the agar.
Incubate plates at one of the following: 37 °C overnight, 30 °C for two days, or room temperature for three days.
